awards.label: Best Overall
awards.why: 4.6 stars from over 4,000 reviews, a listed 656 ft range, IP66 rating, and up to 8 switches per receiver.

awards.label: Best Budget
awards.why: $12.99 for a switch and receiver, with 3,673 reviews and 500+ bought last month.

awards.label: Best for 3-Way
awards.why: The receiver is a rocker that replaces your wall switch, and rolling codes keep neighboring kits from interfering.

awards.label: Best Battery-Free
awards.why: The switch powers itself from the press, so there's never a battery to change. Lists 433 MHz.

products.verdict: The most-reviewed kit with the longest listed range. One receiver takes up to 8 switches for multi-location control.
pros: Switch battery rated for 8 to 10 years
cons: The bullet heading says 5-year warranty, the text says 3-year

products.verdict: A 15 A kit with dynamic codes, so several sets in one house won't trigger each other. Selling fast at 1K+ a month.
pros: Dynamic codes prevent interference between kits
Weatherproof receiver for attics and outdoors
cons: Listed range is 100 ft, shorter than Thinkbee
Needs a neutral at the receiver

products.verdict: The cheapest well-reviewed kit. Fine for a closet, attic, or a fixture with a pull chain.
pros: 3,673 reviews, 500+ bought in the past month
Expandable with more switches, remotes, and receivers of the same model
cons: Rated for only 200 W of LED
Expansion only works with the same model

products.verdict: DEWENWILS' higher-capacity kit, with a 15 A receiver for bigger fixtures.
pros: One switch can control several receivers, or several switches one receiver
cons: Needs a neutral at the receiver

products.verdict: The neatest way to add a second switch location. The receiver replaces your existing wall switch, and the wireless switch goes wherever you want the second one.
pros: Receiver is a rocker that replaces your existing switch
Rolling codes keep multiple kits independent
cons: Needs a neutral in the switch box

products.verdict: A decorator rocker that pops off its plate magnetically, so it doubles as a handheld remote.
pros: Magnetic switch works on the wall or in your hand
4.7 stars, 400+ bought in the past month
cons: Review count is shared with the 3-way version

products.verdict: The 3-way version of treewell's magnetic rocker kit, for a light you want to control from two spots.
pros: Set up for 3-way control out of the box
cons: Review count is shared with the single kit

products.verdict: The press itself powers the switch, so there's no battery to replace. Good for bathrooms and spots you'll forget about.
pros: Waterproof switch for bathrooms and patios
One receiver can take several switch panels

products.verdict: A general-purpose 433 MHz relay kit with momentary, toggle, and latched modes. Useful for tinkerers and non-lighting jobs.
pros: Lists 433 MHz, which makes it a candidate for RF bridges and rtl_433
Three programmable modes: momentary, toggle, latched
cons: The transmitter is a remote, not a wall-style switch

products.verdict: An extra switch for a Thinkbee kit you already own. Pair up to 8 with one receiver for stairs, basements, and garages.
cons: Does nothing without a Thinkbee receiver
Only works with the Thinkbee models listed

avoid.flag: Radio claims don't add up, and it's rated at 1 A
avoid.verdict: The listing can't keep its story straight about how this kit connects, and its own spec table rates it far below the loads it advertises.
reasons: The title says "Support 2.4G&5G" and Alexa compatibility, while a bullet says you connect it to Alexa over Bluetooth.
The spec table lists a 1 A current rating, about 120 W at 120 V, yet the bullets promise up to 200 W of LED and 300 W of halogen.
It needs a neutral wire and dimmable bulbs, both only mentioned deep in the bullets.
The SURAIELEC and DEWENWILS kits above cost the same or less and state 15 A ratings.
